item.statement: Six 60° equilateral triangle central angles meet at the center of a regular hexagon, totaling 360°.

item.rule_text: If three sides of one triangle are equal to three sides of another triangle, the triangles are congruent.
If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to two sides and the included angle of another, the triangles are congruent.
If two angles and one side (included or non-included) of one triangle equal two angles and corresponding side of another, the triangles are congruent.
In two right-angled triangles, if the hypotenuse and one leg of one triangle equal the hypotenuse and one leg of the other, the triangles are congruent.
Multiply factors as whole numbers, then place decimal point so decimal places equal the sum of decimal places in the factors.

item.procedure_name: Solving Linear Equation via Inverse Operations
steps: 1. Identify operations attached to the variable.
2. Apply inverse operations in reverse order to both sides of equation (LHS and RHS).
3. Simplify both sides until variable is isolated on one side.
4. Substitute solution back into original equation to verify LHS = RHS.

item.relationship_name: HCF, LCM, and Product of Two Numbers
item.description: The product of HCF and LCM of any two numbers equals the product of those two numbers.

item.relationship_name: Multiplication and Division as Inverse Operations
item.description: If a × b = c, then c ÷ b = a and c ÷ a = b.

item.relationship_name: Equilateral Triangle Angle and Hexagon Central Angle
item.description: The interior angle of an equilateral triangle (60°) equals the central angle of a regular hexagon, six of which complete a 360° circle.
